Let \(T(V)=V^{\otimes 3}\). First classify the natural endomorphisms of \(T\). If \(\eta:T\Rightarrow T\), evaluate \(\eta\) on \(X=\mathbb F_2^3\) with basis \(x_1,x_2,x_3\). Naturality with projections killing one basis vector forces every term of
\[
\eta_X(x_1\otimes x_2\otimes x_3)
\]
to contain each of \(x_1,x_2,x_3\) exactly once. Hence
\[
\eta_V(v_1\otimes v_2\otimes v_3)
=\sum_{\sigma\in S_3} a_\sigma\,
v_{\sigma(1)}\otimes v_{\sigma(2)}\otimes v_{\sigma(3)}.
\]
So
\[
\operatorname{End}(T)\cong \mathbb F_2[S_3],
\qquad
\operatorname{End}(F)\cong M_3(\mathbb F_2[S_3]).
\]

Let \(c=(123)\) and
\[
z=1+c+c^2\in \mathbb F_2[S_3].
\]
Then \(z\) is a central idempotent, and
\[
\mathbb F_2[S_3]\cong z\mathbb F_2[S_3]\times (1-z)\mathbb F_2[S_3]
\cong \mathbb F_2[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)\times M_2(\mathbb F_2).
\]
Thus an idempotent in \(M_3(\mathbb F_2[S_3])\) has a type \((a,b)\), where
\[
0\le a\le 3,\qquad 0\le b\le 6,
\]
corresponding to rank \(a\) over the local block and ordinary rank \(b\) over \(M_6(\mathbb F_2)\).

Now compute the rank contribution on \(V_n^{\otimes 3}\). The operator \(z=1+c+c^2\) sums over cyclic rotations. On basis triples \((i,j,k)\), the \(C_3\)-orbits have size \(1\) when \(i=j=k\), and size \(3\) otherwise. Therefore
\[
A_n:=\operatorname{rank}(z)=n+\frac{n^3-n}{3}
=\frac{n^3+2n}{3}.
\]
The complementary block has rank
\[
n^3-A_n=\frac{2(n^3-n)}{3},
\]
so one primitive \(M_2\)-block contributes
\[
B_n=\frac{n^3-n}{3}.
\]
Hence an idempotent of type \((a,b)\) has rank
\[
aA_n+bB_n.
\]

The identity has type \((3,6)\), so ranks just below it are found by minimizing the positive deficit
\[
(3-a)A_n+(6-b)B_n.
\]
Since \(A_n=B_n+n\), the smallest positive deficit is \(B_n\), and the next distinct one is \(A_n\) for every \(n\ge2\) (for \(n=2\), \(A_n=2B_n\), giving an extra type).

Thus
\[
R_n^{(1)}=3n^3-B_n=\frac{8n^3+n}{3},
\qquad
R_n^{(2)}=3n^3-A_n=\frac{8n^3-2n}{3}.
\]

Counts: the number of rank \(r\) idempotents in \(M_m(\mathbb F_2)\) is
\[
\binom mr_2 2^{r(m-r)}.
\]
So rank \(5\) idempotents in \(M_6(\mathbb F_2)\) number
\[
\binom65_2 2^5=63\cdot 32=2016.
\]
Hence \(N_n^{(1)}=2016\).

For the local block \(B=\mathbb F_2[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)\),
\[
\#\{\text{rank }2\text{ idempotents in }M_3(B)\}
=
\frac{|\operatorname{GL}_3(B)|}{|\operatorname{GL}_2(B)|\,|\operatorname{GL}_1(B)|}
=448.
\]
So for \(n\ge3\), \(N_n^{(2)}=448\).

When \(n=2\), the second deficit can also be \(2B_n\), giving type \((a,b)=(3,4)\). Rank \(4\) idempotents in \(M_6(\mathbb F_2)\) number
\[
\binom64_2 2^8=651\cdot 256=166656.
\]
Thus
\[
N_2^{(2)}=448+166656=167104.
\]

Final answer:
\[
\boxed{
\left(R_n^{(1)},N_n^{(1)},R_n^{(2)},N_n^{(2)}\right)
=
\begin{cases}
(22,\,2016,\,20,\,167104),& n=2,\\[4pt]
\left(\dfrac{8n^3+n}{3},\,2016,\,
\dfrac{8n^3-2n}{3},\,448\right),& n\ge3.
\end{cases}}
\]
